title: Juniper and the Harbor Revisited
premise: Ines Coldharbour inherited Coldharbour Vineyard along with its crushing debts, and the only way to save it is a lucrative contract with the Meridian Hospitality Group—negotiated by Juniper Vale, the strategist who once walked out of Ines's life without explanation. When Ines is cornered into bringing a date to the Coldharbour family reunion, Juniper impulsively volunteers, and what begins as damage control turns into an evening of dangerous honesty. As the reunion weekend stretches on, old wounds surface: why Juniper left, what Ines sacrificed to keep the vineyard alive, and whether love can survive two people who learned to protect themselves by disappearing. Ines must choose between signing away the vineyard to Meridian—the deal that would erase every debt—and fighting for a future where neither survival nor love has to be a trade-off, ending with them planting new vines together as equal partners in both business and life.
about_author: August Ashgrove is the pen name of a former sommelier who traded tasting notes for love stories set among vines and salt air. They write romances about people who mistake endurance for living.

chapters.title: Debts Instead of Grapes
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines surveys the struggling vineyard, the foreclosure notice pinned to the office door, and the invitation to the Coldharbour reunion demanding they arrive 'with someone worth introducing.' The emotional beat is weary defiance—a person who has stopped hoping but refuses to stop working.

chapters.title: The Stranger at the Tasting Room
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper arrives to assess Coldharbour Vineyard for Meridian's acquisition team and freezes upon recognizing Ines behind the counter. Neither lets on that they know each other. The beat is charged restraint: two people performing professionalism while history hums beneath it.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Over a tense negotiation dinner, Ines learns Juniper holds the fate of the vineyard—and realizes the reunion deadline collides with Meridian's decision week. Juniper offers, half-joking, to be the fake date. The beat is wary humor masking unresolved hurt.

chapters.title: Rehearsing a Lie
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A Sunday spent rehearsing their couple act among the vines—shared jokes, accidental touches, one almost-confession interrupted by a call from Meridian. Ines catalogs all the reasons this can't be real. The beat is longing disguised as logistics.

chapters.title: The Coldharbour Table
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The reunion begins: sharp-tongued aunts, a cousin angling for the estate, and Ines's mother dissecting both the vineyard's failures and Ines's loneliness. Juniper defends Ines too fiercely for a fake date. The beat is protective tenderness turning public.

chapters.title: Too Real by Dessert
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. During dessert, under the table, hands find each other; afterward, on the porch, Juniper nearly explains why they left years ago but retreats when Ines's mother interrupts with news: Meridian wants an answer early. The beat is intimacy interrupted by the ticking clock.

chapters.title: What Survival Cost
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper finally confesses: they left because Ines chose the vineyard over them once before, and Juniper swore never to compete with a debt again. Ines reveals the truth of that night—that they'd been protecting Juniper from the ruin they saw coming. The beat is devastating mutual misunderstanding laid bare.

chapters.title: The Signature
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Meridian presents final papers: sign, and every debt vanishes—but the vineyard, and any future with Juniper inside Meridian's machine, becomes collateral. Ines signs nothing and walks out into the rain. The beat is the quiet terror and freedom of refusing the easy exit.

chapters.title: Harvest Eve
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper burns their bridge—resigning from Meridian, pitching instead a partnership plan to save Coldharbour using their own savings and the family's grudging blessing secured at the reunion. The climax lands as Juniper finds Ines in the storm-damaged fields. The beat is reckless, wholehearted commitment.

chapters.title: New Vines
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Spring: debts restructured, the reunion family rallied, and Ines and Juniper planting rootstock together—no longer invisible, no longer trading survival against love. A final toast with the vineyard's first honest bottle. The beat is earned joy: inheritance reclaimed as something given freely.
